manuscript_claim_lines.ex_ante_claim: A global-games run model (Appendix~\ref{app:model}) yields an ex-ante fragility ordering for the March 2023 shock, driven by reserve exposure: USDC (direct SVB exposure) most fragile, DAI (mechanically pinned to USDC through the PSM) next, and USDT (no SVB exposure) least.
manuscript_claim_lines.realized_ordering_claim: \paragraph{Realized ordering.} Troughs are \$0.877 (USDC), \$0.886 (DAI), and \$0.992 (USDT), matching the ex-ante fragility ordering

claim_type_determination: FULL RANK ORDER over a linked pair and one free coin. The ex-ante paragraph (fc27.tex:482) states an explicit 3-way ranking (USDC most fragile, DAI next, USDT least) and the realized-ordering paragraph (fc27.tex:523) reports the realized troughs as consistent with that ex-ante exposure ranking. DAI is mechanically linked to USDC through the PSM (Appendix B), so it is not an exchangeable draw and the USDC-DAI pair moves as one block. The null space is the 2 placements of USDT relative to that block, not the 6 permutations of 3 free items.

permutations.description: USDT least fragile, outside the linked USDC-DAI block
USDT more fragile than the linked USDC-DAI block

note: 1/2 under the ruled null (D16). The free comparison is USDT against the linked USDC-DAI pair, because Appendix B establishes DAI's break runs through its USDC exposure rather than an independent run. Scoring the match against all 6 permutations would treat DAI as exchangeable, which the paper's own contagion argument denies.
